bug_semantics: RabbitTemplate.sendAndReceive() with a configured fixed reply queue correlates replies by a messageTag written into the AMQP correlationId (or a custom correlation header). That tag was generated from a per-instance AtomicInteger (messageTagProvider.incrementAndGet()), producing sequential, guessable identifiers that restart at 1 on each new RabbitTemplate. Two templates sharing one reply queue therefore overlap in identifier space; an actor who can publish to that queue can inject a forged reply or steal a legitimate one before the real response arrives (CWE-330 reply poisoning). The same counter also tagged the temporary-queue path; the CVE attack is the shared fixed-queue case. userCorrelationId only opts out when the caller already supplied a unique id.
flaw_origin: AMQP-206 (fd696bfaf97bfe28fc4fa5f7181169ccef5d05e1, 2012-01-11) first added doSendAndReceiveWithFixed using UUID.randomUUID() as the correlation tag. AMQP-507 (0a11c54328bf4d63beb8be609a84c0297b401ecc, 2015-06-27) replaced that UUID with a new AtomicInteger messageTagProvider so send-and-reply could attach a compact RETURN_CORRELATION_KEY for mandatory publisher returns; both the fixed and temporary paths then called incrementAndGet(). Later listener-path refactors (AMQP-655, AMQP-779, GH-1181) moved the increment into doSendAndReceiveAsListener but kept the same sequential counter. GH-3470 restored UUID.randomUUID() in 2026.

reasoning: The CVE is a real CWE-330 in Spring AMQP: fixed-reply-queue sendAndReceive correlated replies with a process-local AtomicInteger, so tags were sequential and collided across RabbitTemplate instances that shared a reply queue. Public CVE.org is PUBLISHED and the Spring advisory is not withdrawn, so this is not FALSE_POSITIVE. The smallest first-write of that sequential-tag mechanism is 0a11c54328bf4d63beb8be609a84c0297b401ecc (AMQP-507, 2015). Its parent 5ce03d0d19892bae172c7fe892aee6278ec4f831 still used UUID.randomUUID() in doSendAndReceiveWithFixed (the 2012 AMQP-206 design) and has no messageTagProvider. 0a11c543 is a single-parent JIRA commit, not a merge/squash/move/revert; later AMQP-655/779 and GH-1181 only relocated the same incrementAndGet into doSendAndReceiveAsListener. That BIC is an ancestor of every listed affected OSS tag (2.4.0+, 3.1.0+, 3.2.0-3.2.10, 4.0.0-4.0.3). GH-3470 ca163ae82281e979d4cf3a93ba51829aabbe3b59 on main restores UUID and is the originating code fix; identical cherry-picks land at the OSS patched boundaries v4.0.4 and v3.2.11.
